## K7 · K7-Q4-pid-boot-split — pid-pool-pinning: F1 counting vs the boot process split

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 6

Decision references: docs/kernel/processes.md, docs/kernel/budgets.md#r10-destruction

Evidence: architect-2 decided: a held PID counts once in the budget the process runs in, until its object is freed; on that budget's destruction the count moves to its parent after the carve returns (R10 step 8); boot split stays 15/48. Written on docs/kernel/processes.md, budgets.md, invariants.md I10 and todo/pid-pool-pinning.md, committed 58f13ec98. K7 builds it.

### Implementer · Question

> Blocking (pid-pool-pinning only). Page: docs/kernel/budgets.md, the boot table: system 15 processes, users 48, root keeps 0.
> 
> Under F1 a created PID counts in its creator's budget. Today the first program (the stand-in for init, which also launches the benches) runs in system, so everything it creates counts against system's 15, less the loader programs themselves. sched-debt-lift starts 19 children at once, and sched-latency starts the driver, the steward and the spinners. Both now fail with OutOfProcesses at spawn. Every other process-creating case passes on rv64 once proc-attack and proc-test expect the new counts.
> 
> The same problem is in the planned design. init runs in root, which keeps 0 processes, and the steward creates principals' processes, so under F1 those count in system-class creators, not in users.
> 
> Options:
> (A, recommended) Flip the boot split: system gets three quarters (47) and users a quarter (15). Under F1 the creators are system-class (init, the steward), and the budgets.md table and figure change with it. When init moves to root (M1), root keeps its share. I note that on the page as planned, not built.
> (B) Keep 15/48 and cut the two sched cases to at most 13 concurrent children. That weakens debt-lift's N=16 and caps the first program at about 13 children.
> (C) Revisit F1, for example by counting in both budgets. The todo rejects that because it halves the machine's processes.
> 
> I continue meanwhile with the model, the pid-pinning-attack case and the pages, and hold the commit for your ruling.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `c9d51af7d6319e055e31146ccb5e47f8` · 2026-09-28T08:34:21Z

> K7 Q4 (thread K7-Q4-pid-boot-split; read the implementer's question on it). Background: your predecessor ruled (thread k7-f1-pid-double-count, committed 068a3e6ff) that a created process's PID counts once, in its CREATOR's budget's process limit, from process_create until its object is freed (so destroying a child budget cannot drop a count while an untaken notice still pins the PID). Consequence found in K7: the boot split on docs/kernel/budgets.md gives system 15 processes and users 48, but every creator today and in the planned design is system-class (the first program/init, the steward creating principals' sessions), so creations hit system's 15; two sched cases now fail at spawn. Implementer's options: (A, recommended by it) flip the split, system 47 / users 15; (B) keep 15/48 and cut the cases to <=13 children; (C) revisit F1 (count twice), rejected before. My concern with (A): if the steward creates every principal's session processes, their PIDs all count in the steward's own (system) limit, so PID fairness across principals rests on the steward's own quotas, and one principal who makes the steward create many processes could spend PIDs every other principal needs. Is that the intended rule (the steward already meters principals, R26-style), or should a created PID count in the budget it is created into, moving to the creator's budget if that budget is destroyed while the PID is still held (so the pinning attack stays closed)? Decide; write the rule and the boot split on budgets.md/processes.md (main checkout, docs only, don't stage); answer on the thread. K7 holds that commit meanwhile.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `579113ed021f396bba5dd7bb5e21340c` · 2026-09-28T08:37:38Z

> Decided: none of A/B/C. A held PID counts once, in the budget the process RUNS IN, for as long as the PID is held. Not an owner choice: no wall moves, and this protects separation. F1's single count and the closed pinning attack both stand.
> 
> Rule: a created process counts from process_create until its object is freed; a loader-started program counts while it lives. Who launched it doesn't matter. If that budget is destroyed while the PID is still held (killed, and its creator outside the destroyed tree hasn't taken the notice), R10 step 8 moves the count to B's parent after the carve returns, as it moves quarantined DMA pages. The PIDs were inside the carve, so the parent can't go over its limit.
> 
> Why not the creator (your concern is right): init and the steward launch everyone's processes, so every principal's PIDs would pool in one system budget. One principal could spend the others' PIDs, and a vault session's steward-started launches would show on its unlabelled side (R37). Why not move to the creator on destruction: it may be at its limit (I5).
> 
> Boot split stays 15/48. debt-lift's spinners run under USERS, so they fit. Planned tree: root keeps one process for init.
> 
> Residual, stated: a creator's untaken notices hold PIDs in a budget it was given, bounded by that budget's limit. A budget handle is already the right to spend it.
> 
> Written (main checkout, unstaged): docs/kernel/processes.md, docs/kernel/budgets.md (the processes row, R6, R10 steps 7-8, Failure, residual, Why, planned tree), docs/kernel/invariants.md (I10 residual), docs/todo/pid-pool-pinning.md (What, Where, Done when: count until freed, the destruction move, the attack case plus a mutation for each). mdbook exit 0, doccheck exit 0.
> 
> For K7: the kernel already checks the target budget. Keep the count until the object is freed, add the step-8 move, and put the limit check before the PID draw.

> Q4 decided (supersedes F1's 'creator' wording; F1's single count stands): a held PID counts once, in the budget the process RUNS IN, from process_create until its object is freed (a loader-started program while it lives). If that budget is destroyed while the PID is still held, R10 step 8 moves the count to its parent after the carve returns (like quarantined DMA pages). Boot split stays 15/48 (debt-lift's spinners run under users, so they fit). Pages rewritten on redoubt: docs/kernel/processes.md, budgets.md (processes row, R6, R10 steps 7-8, residual, Why), invariants.md I10, and docs/todo/pid-pool-pinning.md's Done when (count until freed, the destruction move, the attack case plus a mutation for each). Kernel: it already checks the target budget; keep the count until the object is freed, add the step-8 move, put the limit check before the PID draw. Rebase onto redoubt before committing pid-pool (between commits). Red finding 3 ('creator means creator's budget') no longer applies.
